Trace the water route before choosing a repair.

We investigate the reported leak before selecting a repair. The visible stain, the roof above it and the drainage route can tell different parts of the story. We connect those observations, define accessible investigation and set out the material and access requirements for the agreed work.

01 / Metal roof edge and cladding junction

Tell us when the water appears

Compare the timing and position of a ceiling mark with the roof junctions upwind and the outlets downhill. Allow separately for clearing restricted flow, repairing a known failed flashing, and opening any concealed wet substrate. A new bead of sealant is not a scope for the whole route.

We start with the location and time of the indoor mark, the last weather event and the areas served by the nearest outlets. We record a visible defect, a suspected water route and a confirmed repair separately, so a patch does not close out an unresolved leak.

  • During particular rain or wind

    We record the affected rooms, weather conditions and previous repairs, then inspect accessible roof details and drainage. The stain location alone does not identify the entry point.

  • Near roof equipment or junctions

    Inspect penetrations, flashings, adjoining sheets and fixings together to account for neighbouring deterioration and connected water paths.

  • Overflow or water below a terrace

    We distinguish roof drainage from balcony or terrace waterproofing. Outlets, surface falls, joints and the existing waterproofing build-up inform the investigation scope.

  • When a cleared gutter still overflows

    We follow runoff from the roof valleys, laps and flashings around penetrations to the gutter, outlet, downpipe and downstream collection point. A clear gutter can still overflow where an outlet is restricted or the downstream system backs up. Dripping after the rain has stopped is useful timing evidence: water may still be draining along concealed layers away from the point of entry.

02 / Interior signs of water entry

Compatibility belongs in the specification

  • Metal roofs and drainage

    We identify the existing metal, coating, fasteners and adjoining materials. Exposed and sheltered coastal locations inform the condition assessment; product guidance applies to the actual material being used.

  • Waterproofing layers

    We confirm the existing system, substrate and relevant junctions before defining repairs. Surface finishes, removal and reinstatement are itemised where they form part of the work.

A repair sequence tied to the fault

If a ceiling mark grows during wind-driven rain, record the windward wall, the nearest roof junction and where the outlet discharges. Timing and location help narrow the inspection before any internal finish is reinstated.

  1. 01

    Investigate and record

    We map the reported leak and accessible defects, identifying any investigation that needs separate access or opening-up.

  2. 02

    Prepare and repair

    We prepare the agreed area, address the specified detail and connect the repair to sound retained material using the confirmed system.

  3. 03

    Check and document

    We complete the checks appropriate to the agreed scope and record treated locations, junctions and follow-up observations.

Plan the roof and the occupied space below

Height, roof access, weather and the space below all affect staging. We agree material movement, work-area separation and protection for stock, rooms or workstations. Any temporary arrangement and subsequent interior repairs are identified in the scope rather than assumed to be part of the roof item.

We separate clearing a restricted outlet, renewing a failed joint and replacing a damaged gutter section. Repeated backing up may need a wider drainage review. Where the entry point is still open to question, we record what was accessible and agree the next inspection. Roof access, exclusion below, stock protection and the forecast affect staging. The handover identifies cleared outlets, repaired locations and any follow-up after rain.

What we need to price the work

  • Extent and access

    Repair area, roof geometry, height, equipment access and the extent of concealed deterioration affect the work required.

  • Related work

    We identify gutter cleaning, drainage repairs, removal, waste and internal reinstatement separately when they are part of the brief.

Record the point repaired and what remains to check.

We identify the sections attended and agree the next rainfall observation before deciding when to reinstate sensitive interior finishes.

  • Leak history and weather
  • Outlet and repair locations
  • Follow-up before reinstatement

Common questions

Common questions

Why can a leak return after sealant was applied?+

Check the earlier patch against the entry point, adjoining components, drains and substrate before defining the repair.

Why does a gutter overflow after it has been cleared?+

Clearing the channel is one step. We also check the outlet, downpipe and downstream route. We price a local repair separately from work to address repeated backing up.

Can the premises remain occupied?+

We assess access, the area below the work and weather-sensitive stages with your manager. The plan identifies usable areas, necessary closures and any interior protection or separate attendance.

Does a leaking commercial roof always need replacing?+

We assess the roof condition, the leak source and the extent of deterioration first. We then set out whether a local repair, a wider repair scope or replacement addresses the problem, with the relevant access and material requirements.
